VERIFIED: The parameter matrix processed 106 retained images across five fresh OpenCV parameter objects and four preprocessing branches without camera or TCP access.
Widening the adaptive threshold window was the only tested parameter family that materially recovered dynamic failure thumbnails: blue 2x detected 4/6 versus 0/6 for the default gray 1x control.
The same adaptive-wide candidate exceeded the 33.333333 ms budget on both dynamic and static samples.
Subpixel refinement, contour refinement, and relaxed perimeter did not recover the six dynamic failure thumbnails on the gray 1x branch.
INFERENCE: Adaptive threshold coverage is a plausible contributor to the OpenCV candidate rejection pattern, but the evidence does not establish that it is the only cause.
Applying adaptive-wide only inside the existing ROI may preserve some of its recovery benefit at lower cost than a full-frame adaptive pass; this is a new offline hypothesis, not a verified fix.
INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE: Six dynamic failure thumbnails are not enough to claim a production detection improvement or B3 readiness.
No candidate in this matrix satisfies detection continuity and the 33.333333 ms p95 budget simultaneously.
No production PoseTracker, firmware, calibration, or hardware behavior was changed by this experiment.

decision.next_offline_action: Benchmark an adaptive-wide preprocessing pass constrained to the existing ROI, with the current gray ROI path as control and an explicit per-frame time budget.
